title: About
text:
I’m interested in applying data science to practical problems—combining statistical thinking, machine learning, and strong analytical workflows.
My portfolio is a place to document not only finished projects, but also the reasoning behind them: how I prepare data, choose evaluation metrics, compare approaches, and communicate limitations.
I choose projects based on my interests and the opportunity to learn new skills. I enjoy exploring new datasets, asking questions, and finding ways to answer them with data. I also love film, economics, outdoor activities such as skiing and mountaineering, and try to reflect those interests in my projects when possible.

title: Projects
text:
Goal: Recommend movies that fit a user’s taste using their own personal rating history from their Letterboxd profile.
Purpose: Letterboxd currently does not have an algorithmic recommendation feature to suggest relevant movies to its users. Other media services such as Spotify and Netflix have award winning recommendation systems and do not need to be improved upon. The lack of this feature within letterboxd presents a unique opportunity to develop one for a very popular application with many users and many ratings / reviews. I also am an avid user of Letterboxd (as are many of my friends), so this is an especially interesting project for me. There is a case to be made that Letterboxd not having an algorithmic feed / recommendation feature is refreshing to its users as the point of the app is to log your own ratings and see what your friends are watching / liking. This is why this is simply a project for my friends and I to use out of curiosity or help us pick movies!
Approach: Compare collaborative-filtering models with content-based signals from movie metadata. Evaluate ranked recommendations, not only rating prediction error.
Next steps: Finish offline training, add a content-based fallback for newer films, and connect the model to a Streamlit demo.
Tools: Python · Pandas · scikit-surprise · TMDB API · Streamlit
GitHub repository · Live demo
